title: Update methods only save already-tracked SwiftData objects

evidence.quote: Feed is already tracked by the context, just save
Digest is already tracked by the context, just save

reasoning: The public repository protocols accept a model and promise to update an existing entity, but both implementations only call save() and rely on the passed object already being tracked by the same ModelContext. Passing a detached object, an object from another context, or a freshly constructed value with the same identity will not update the persisted row as the protocol suggests.
reproduction: Persist a Feed, create a separate Feed with the same url and changed properties, call updateFeed(_:) on it, then fetch by url; the stored feed remains unchanged because the repository never looks it up or applies fields.
recommendation: Either make the contract explicit that update requires a tracked object from this repository context, or implement updates by fetching the persisted entity by id/url and copying mutable fields before saving.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked update tests mutate the exact object that was inserted into the same context, so they only cover the tracked-object path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add update tests that pass a detached Feed/Digest with the same identifier and assert the stored entity is updated, or add tests documenting that detached updates are rejected with a clear error.
